Added an audit_log table and row-level PostgreSQL triggers so that every insert, update or delete on users or feeds appends an audit row. The existing build, unit tests and integration tests pass; the new behaviour itself has not been exercised by any test I could run.

- **Migration** (`internal/database/migrations.go`): creates `audit_log` (`id`, `created_at`, `table_name`, `operation`, `row_id`), a trigger function, and AFTER INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE triggers on `users` and `feeds`.
- **Last-login exception** (`internal/storage/user.go`): `SetLastLogin` now runs in a transaction that sets a transaction-local flag (`miniflux.skip_audit`), which the trigger checks and skips. Nothing else is exempt.

Things to know:

- **Schema is my own choice.** There was no existing `audit_log` definition in the repository, so the column names are my choice; acceptance tests expecting different columns would fail.
- **Not limited to API requests.** Because this is done in the database, changes from the web UI, the background feed scheduler and the CLI are logged too. Bulk operations write one row per affected feed or user, including cascaded feed deletions when a user is removed.
- **No acting user recorded.** The trigger cannot see who made the request; adding that would need the user ID plumbed through the storage calls.
- **Row contents are not copied.** Both tables hold credentials, so the log records only which row changed and how.

- **Last-login exception** (`internal/storage/user.go`): `SetLastLogin` now runs in a transaction that sets a transaction-local flag (`miniflux.skip_audit`), which the trigger checks and skips. Nothing else is exempt.

Things to know:

- **Schema is my own choice.** There was no existing `audit_log` definition in the repository, so the column names are my choice; acceptance tests expecting different columns would fail.
- **Not limited to API requests.** Because this is done in the database, changes from the web UI, the background feed scheduler and the CLI are logged too. Bulk operations write one row per affected feed or user, including cascaded feed deletions when a user is removed.
- **No acting user recorded.** The trigger cannot see who made the request; adding that would need the user ID plumbed through the storage calls.
- **Row contents are not copied.** Both tables hold credentials, so the log records only which row changed and how.
